references.text: Moses mustered the Levites according to the Lord's command, demonstrating the same pattern of obedience to God's instruction.
Moses mustered the Israelites in the wilderness of Sinai as the Lord had commanded him, parallel to the numbering of the firstborn.
God's command to consecrate all the firstborn in Israel, which forms the basis for the census Moses carries out.
The laws concerning the firstborn who belong to the Lord, explaining why the firstborn had to be counted.
The immediate context where the Lord commands Moses to count every male firstborn in Israel.
The result of the census that Moses conducted, where the number of firstborn is given as 22,273.
The tenth plague at Passover, where Egypt's firstborn were struck down, serving as the historical background for why Israel's firstborn belong to the Lord.
The Lord explains that He took the Levites in place of all the firstborn in Israel after striking down the firstborn in Egypt.
